cross_references.note: §504 and ADA Title II cover overlapping territory for state and local government programs. Always plead both: Title II applies to all public entities; §504 applies to all federal funding recipients. A state agency or court that is both a public entity (Title II) and a federal funding recipient (§504) is covered by both. The standards are similar post-ADAAA but the mechanisms differ (Title II: public entity mandate; §504: federal funds condition).

§504 incorporates ADA standards (§794(d) for employment; case law for program access). ADA violation = Unruh per se (§51(f)). Therefore §504 violation → ADA standard violated → Unruh per se → $4,000 minimum statutory damages in California civil court. The chain: §504 establishes the federal violation; §51(f) converts it to California statutory damages.

DDS (Disability Determination Services) administers SSA disability determinations under contract — receiving federal funding. If DDS excluded or denied benefits to a qualified disabled individual based on phantom contacts or fabricated records, §504 is violated. The §504 track is civil rights; the §405(g) track is administrative review. Both may apply to a deficient DDS determination.

CalVCB administers the federal-state Crime Victims Compensation Program — receiving VOCA (Victims of Crime Act) federal funding. CalVCB is a §504-covered program. Disability-based discrimination in the CalVCB application/appeal process violates §504. Plead alongside the GOV §13950 et seq. statutory violations and the §1094.5 administrative mandamus challenge.

Hospitals and health plans receiving Medicare/Medicaid are §504-covered programs. Denial of medically necessary care to a disabled person by a Medicare/Medicaid-receiving provider is both a Knox-Keene Act violation and a §504 violation. The §504 track adds federal civil rights enforcement to the insurance regulatory track.
